name: GE90–115B powerplant
purpose: A high-bypass, two-spool turbofan developed for the Boeing 777–300ER.
relationship: 22 fan blades · 4 booster stages · 9 HPC stages · 2 HPT stages · 6 LPT stages.

name: Exterior assembly
purpose: The inlet, acoustic lining and nacelle guide incoming air and enclose the bypass path.
relationship: Stationary structure around the fan and core. The outer duct carries bypass air to its own nozzle.

name: Fan module
purpose: Twenty-two swept composite blades accelerate a large mass of air. Most of that air travels around the core.
relationship: Directly connected to the low-pressure shaft and six-stage LP turbine; no reduction gearbox.

name: Low-pressure compressor
purpose: Four booster stages compress the portion of fan air entering the engine core.
relationship: Rotors turn with the fan and LP turbine. Interleaved stators remain fixed.

name: High-pressure compressor
purpose: Nine axial stages progressively raise the pressure of the core airflow.
relationship: The high-pressure shaft couples these rotors to the two-stage HP turbine. Front stators can change incidence.

name: Combustion system
purpose: Fuel burns continuously inside an annular liner. Cooling and dilution air protect the liner and shape the turbine inlet flow.
relationship: Stationary between the compressor diffuser and HP turbine nozzle guide vanes.

name: High-pressure turbine
purpose: Two turbine stages extract energy from the hot core stream to drive the high-pressure compressor.
relationship: Shares the HP spool with the nine-stage compressor. Nozzle guide vanes direct gas onto the rotors.

name: Low-pressure turbine
purpose: Six turbine stages recover more gas energy to drive the large fan and four-stage booster.
relationship: Connected to the fan through the inner, concentric low-pressure shaft.

name: Shafts & bearings
purpose: Two concentric shaft systems transmit torque while bearings locate and support the rotating assemblies.
relationship: The inner LP shaft runs through the hollow HP shaft. The two spools turn independently.

name: Auxiliary systems
purpose: A representative accessory gearbox, starter, oil system, control unit and harness serve the engine.
relationship: Accessory routing and hardware are illustrative; external line segments terminate at fittings.

purpose: A rounded inlet lip guides air smoothly toward the fan.
relationship: Surrounds the 128-inch fan. Its profile is an educational nacelle approximation.

name: GE90–115B powerplant
purpose: A high-bypass, two-spool turbofan developed for the Boeing 777–300ER.
relationship: 22 fan blades · 4 booster stages · 9 HPC stages · 2 HPT stages · 6 LPT stages.

name: Exterior assembly
purpose: The inlet, acoustic lining and nacelle guide incoming air and enclose the bypass path.
relationship: Stationary structure around the fan and core. The outer duct carries bypass air to its own nozzle.

name: Fan module
purpose: Twenty-two swept composite blades accelerate a large mass of air. Most of that air travels around the core.
relationship: Directly connected to the low-pressure shaft and six-stage LP turbine; no reduction gearbox.

name: Low-pressure compressor
purpose: Four booster stages compress the portion of fan air entering the engine core.
relationship: Rotors turn with the fan and LP turbine. Interleaved stators remain fixed.

name: High-pressure compressor
purpose: Nine axial stages progressively raise the pressure of the core airflow.
relationship: The high-pressure shaft couples these rotors to the two-stage HP turbine. Front stators can change incidence.

name: Combustion system
purpose: Fuel burns continuously inside an annular liner. Cooling and dilution air protect the liner and shape the turbine inlet flow.
relationship: Stationary between the compressor diffuser and HP turbine nozzle guide vanes.

name: High-pressure turbine
purpose: Two turbine stages extract energy from the hot core stream to drive the high-pressure compressor.
relationship: Shares the HP spool with the nine-stage compressor. Nozzle guide vanes direct gas onto the rotors.

name: Low-pressure turbine
purpose: Six turbine stages recover more gas energy to drive the large fan and four-stage booster.
relationship: Connected to the fan through the inner, concentric low-pressure shaft.

name: Shafts & bearings
purpose: Two concentric shaft systems transmit torque while bearings locate and support the rotating assemblies.
relationship: The inner LP shaft runs through the hollow HP shaft. The two spools turn independently.
